_comment: WC2026 Round of 32, 2026-07-03, Vancouver. KNOCKOUT: no draw -- level after 90' -> extra time -> penalties, so the deliverable is who ADVANCES. Routes: Switzerland WON Group B (1-1 Qatar, 4-1 Bosnia, 2-1 Canada; 7 pts, GF 7 GA 3, rating 81) -- balanced and attacking (7 goals), won the group, but NOT airtight (GA 3, conceded in all three) and can be held by a block (1-1 Qatar). Algeria qualified as a BEST THIRD from Group J (0-3 Argentina, 2-1 Jordan, 3-3 Austria; 4 pts, GF 5 GA 7, GD -2, rating 76) -- ATTACKING (5 goals, a wild 3-3 with Austria) but VERY LEAKY (shipped 3 to both Argentina and Austria, GA 7). Class gap ~5 (81 vs 76) -> Switzerland a MODERATE favourite. KEY texture: like the round's other open ties (USA-Bosnia, Belgium-Senegal), Algeria is an ATTACKING, very leaky side, NOT a low block -> an open, higher-scoring, BTTS/Over-live game (a favourite+goals lean), not a containment grind. Switzerland the favourite by class and the more balanced side; Algeria a dangerous, leaky underdog that can score (and did, 5 goals, incl. a 3-3) but concedes freely. Modest shootout risk. Home = Switzerland (nominal; neutral venue). Cards not modelled (referee TBD).

_postmatch.verdict: Clean process hit on side and margin. Switzerland advanced as the 67.0% pick, won 2-0 (a top-4 scoreline at 8.5%), and kept a clean sheet -- xG 1.85 -> 2 goals, on the nose. The one lean that missed is the BTTS: I read this as an OPEN, both-score game (BTTS 58%, Over 58%) given Algeria's attack (5 goals) and Switzerland's non-airtight defence (GA 3) -- but Algeria, the very-leaky underdog, was shut out (the BTTS-No / clean-sheet branch, ~32%, not the central 58% lean). So the SIDE, MARGIN and advancement were all right, but the game was cleaner at the back than the end-to-end texture I sketched. NOTABLY this is the SECOND open-archetype tie in a row where the favourite kept a clean sheet against a leaky, attacking underdog (USA 2-0 Bosnia, now Switzerland 2-0 Algeria) -- both times I leaned BTTS-Yes and both times the underdog didn't score.
_postmatch.lesson: Recurring correction: in the 'favourite vs open/leaky underdog' archetype I have been OVER-leaning BTTS-Yes. Twice now (USA 2-0 Bosnia, Switzerland 2-0 Algeria) the leaky attacking underdog was actually SHUT OUT -- the favourite's edge showed at BOTH ends, not just in attack. A leaky underdog concedes freely but that does NOT guarantee it scores; when the favourite controls the game it can also blank them. Trust the clean-sheet probability (Switzerland 32%) as a real branch, not a minority story -- the 2-0/2-1/1-0 clean-favourite-win cluster is heavier than a naive 'both teams are leaky so both score' read suggests. Side and margin were right; temper the BTTS lean in this archetype.
